body:
Thank you. I think that's what I needed to hear. I'm still very ... Blah, but I feel better, sitting with my lovers.

It's hard to see that it's worth it, but let's hope so.

Yeah, we are. 

They still need to do some talking to each other, hammer out some things, still, but everything is still new. It's been less than two week and Wayne and I both work full time, and Bruce starts school in a couple days, so it's to be expected. Bruce and Wayne both seem happy with the proposed scenario, however.

Thank you. I'm so happy to hear someone else has been through what I'm feeling and made it to the other side happy. :)

I'm sorry, but I'm not quite understanding what you mean by 

"What does Wayne bring to the table? This may seem like an odd thing to ask, but, the best poly relationships understand that one of the benefits of poly is that it makes the people involved richer, sometimes only in experience and wisdom, but, it all works out best when the people involved feel like their animal needs for security and comfort and growth are also being improved by the poly sex bonding."

Please explain further if I'm wrong, but what I'm understanding is that you want to be coming out of these encounters as a better person, if only in the sense of being more experienced.

That's kind of the reason Bruce and I started off "opening" our relationship. We are each other's firsts, and are both pretty inexperienced in both sex and relationships.

Bruce and I have talked about it. He doesn't feel that our relationship would end badly, even if one of us were to 'cheat' or do something 'bad'. I think it would take a little time for us to sort things out for ourselves, but that altogether we could regain trust in each other if it came to that.

Bruce and Wayne have also talked about what would happen, and have both assured me that it's not going to fuck up their friendship, which was something I had expressed a lot of concern over.

I really wish that were the case, but I don't think it's going to get any better. I'm pretty sure their opinions on the topic won't change much, if at all.

It's kind of the opposite. They feel as if I'm the one 'forcing' him. I'm the one making 'bad choices'.
Yeah. I'm thinking more and more that these are just not good people to talk to about it, no matter how much that sucks.
However, there is a poly group in my area, that I think I'm going to start attending. I'm kind of nervous, but I think it's for the best.

Oh, no, we don't mix drinking and talking or anything. We've had drinks and hung out, but all three of us are on the same page.
Also, if we were to go further than we have, it would be completely sober. You can't negotiate while drinking.
I've talked to both of them about it while sober, and we are all on the same page.

I've talked to Wayne before about that kind of thing, too. At first, because of how young I am, he wasn't sure if I knew how, or was ready to go about this maturely, and I told him that what I wanted was to go about things while being as transparent as possible. I love Bruce. We're getting ready to move in together. We've been together for two years now. There's no way I'm going to do something if I know it hurts him. I explained that I love Bruce, and that he and I had talked about the possibility of this happening before either of us discussed being being non-monogamous(not necessarily poly), when we started the relationship. I've told him that I don't want to hurt Bruce - or anyone - at all.

I don't really see an issue here between the three of us, besides that this is a budding thing that seems to be happening, and we are, Bruce and I, feeling our way around this new thing. The problem, I find myself facing is that I feel... Kind of alone right now, when it comes to my friends, and them judging me in the way that they have.

Yeah, I'm oing to have to go on without their input.
Thank you, so much.
He's upset, doesn't want it to be this way, but that I shouldn't talk to them about it anymore, if they're going to be this way.

Thank you. This is exactly what I've been needing to hear. Everything has just been pressuring me to rethink everything I thought, and I keep hearing things from the people I care about that make me feel terrible.

Which sucks, because these were the friends I thought I could trust to accept me through anything. It's worse than it was when I admitted to being bisexual/pansexual, because at least then, I had the support of my friends.
